q: 1. In pile foundation when the load is supported by friction between the pile and surrounding soil and also by resting the pile on hard stratum, such a pile is known as ..........
explain: Most piles rely on a combination of skin friction along the sides and end-bearing at the tip.

q: 2. A type of foundation in which a cantilever beam is used for joining the two footings is ..........
explain: A strap footing connects two individual footings with a rigid beam (strap), often used when one footing is on a property line.

q: 3. For supporting a heavy structure in a sandy soil, the type of foundation generally preferred is ..........
explain: A raft (mat) foundation covers the entire area under the building, which helps reduce differential settlement in sandy or weak soils.

q: 4. The depth of excavation for foundation is usually checked with a ..........
explain: Boning rods are T-shaped wooden rods used in sets to maintain or check the correct levels and depths of trenches.

q: 5. Pile are usually not made of ..........
explain: Stainless steel is too expensive for structural foundation piles; standard steel, timber, and reinforced concrete are used instead.

q: 6. Different types of pitched roofs are ...........
explain: Pitched roofs are categorized by their shape and slope; Gable roofs have two sloping sides meeting at a ridge, while Mansard roofs have four sides with two different slopes on each side.

q: 7. A temporary rigid structure having platforms to enable masons to work at different stages of a building is known as ...........
explain: Scaffolding is the temporary framework used to support workers and materials during construction or repair.

q: 8. The arrangement of supporting an existing structure by providing supports underneath, is known as ...........
explain: Underpinning is the process of strengthening or deepening the foundation of an existing building or structure.
